newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cabinet approves Thai Airways 5-yr plan.
newsitem.headline: Cabinet approves Thai Airways 5-yr plan.

text.p: The Thai cabinet on Tuesday confirmed it had approved Thai Airways International Plc's 1996-2000 business plan, including its acquisition of 21 new airplanes.

Transport and Communications Minister Suwat Liptapallop said the cabinet assigned his ministry to coordinate with the Finance Ministry to work out financing details of the 21 aircraft, estimated to cost 68 billion baht ($2.6 billion).
"The finance and communications ministries would review options of buying or leasing the 21 planes, which will depend on economic and financial conditions," he said.

In January, the cabinet instructed the national carrier to lease, rather than buy, six new aircraft -- which do not fall under the 1996-2000 plan -- that Thai Airways was due to take delivery of this year. The decision was designed to help the country narrow its current account deficit.
Suwat said the leasing decision would save Thailand about eight billion baht in foreign exchange in the short term.
He said his ministry would weigh a proposal by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan for Thai Airways to increase capital in order to raise funds for its expansion.
The Finance Ministry, which holds about 93 percent of Thai Airways shares, has not fixed a time-frame for the capital hike.
